macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC held rates at 3.5%–3.75% on April 29, 2026 (Powell's likely final meeting as chair) in an unusually divided 8-4 vote; one dissenter wanted a cut, three opposed an easing bias. Market pricing zero moves for all of 2026 and only one 25bp cut in December 2027, with elevated inflation partly tied to energy and Middle East uncertainty.
macro_context.geopolitical: US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption risk is the dominant market driver; UAE intercepted Iranian missiles on May 4 in the first activation of its missile-defense system since the recent ceasefire began. IMF projects 3.1% global growth and 4.4% inflation for 2026 under a moderate energy-shock scenario. Tariff uncertainty, new Fed leadership transition, and US midterm elections add additional volatility.

web_context.competitor_activity: Key competitors are Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and Micron Technology. Samsung and SK Hynix are exercising disciplined capex in NAND, supporting pricing; SK Hynix is pivoting heavily toward HBM, leaving enterprise SSD share for SanDisk. Micron is also emphasizing HBM over commodity NAND, further ceding NAND ground to SNDK. Both Micron and SanDisk rallied on CNBC-reported expectations that memory demand will remain elevated through 2030. SanDisk's pure-play NAND positioning (spun off from Western Digital in 2025) is a differentiator vs. Micron's diversified DRAM/HBM/NAND mix. Long-term supply agreements signed by hyperscalers signal industry-wide demand conviction.
